evidence: Receiving DO2 minimum observed ~9.2 mg/L (24-27 h), current ~11.7 mg/L at 52 h, vs 2.0 mg/L constraint floor
Receiving P(48 h)=3.16 g/L vs source-1/2/3 at 48 h: 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L
Receiving assay available at 52 h (sample time 48 h), consistent with healthy source production ramp
Source trajectories show DO2 staying well above 7 mg/L through 96 h while P reaches ~8 g/L, implying no future oxygen-constraint violation
DO2 dip timing and recovery pattern at ~28 h in receiving matches all three sources, indicating normal process replication
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation is performing at or slightly above the healthy source-reference band: P at 48 h is 3.16 g/L vs 2.98-3.06 g/L across the three sources, and DO2 (~11.7 mg/L at 52 h, minimum ~9.2 mg/L) is far above the 2.0 mg/L oxygen constraint. Phase timing and DO2 signatures replicate the sources, with no anomaly. Any feed reduction or stop would sacrifice product mass without addressing a real constraint; increasing aeration is unnecessary given large DO2 headroom. No intervention is the bounded-optimal choice.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters may differ from source parameters; if the receiving process has a lower oxygen transfer capacity or faster OUR than the sources imply, DO2 could fall faster later in the batch, but the observed margin (~7 mg/L above floor) is large relative to that risk. Product degradation past the assay horizon is also possible but not evidenced.
